[PR #2886](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/pull/2886) changes the evidence Boss requires before replacing or restarting an engine: an unavailable fingerprint no longer counts as a version mismatch, and a single failed liveness check no longer schedules recovery.

**1. Problem being solved.** There are two paths where uncertain observations could trigger unnecessary intervention:

- **During startup:** Boss discovers a reachable engine and requests its binary fingerprint. Previously, three unsuccessful requests fell through to the same shutdown-and-replacement path as a confirmed fingerprint mismatch. A busy engine could therefore be stopped even though Boss had no evidence that its build was wrong.
- **During supervision:** the first failed liveness tick immediately consumed a restart attempt and scheduled recovery. The log described this as “engine exited,” although the observation established only unreachability.

The consequences differ: the startup path explicitly stops the existing engine; supervised recovery calls `start()` again, which rediscovers any reachable engine before deciding what to do. See the [previous startup decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L188-L203) and [previous supervisor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift).

**2. Core implementation.** The central fix is an early return when the running engine’s fingerprint remains unavailable. The three attempts, each with a three-second timeout argument, remain unchanged. After those attempts, startup now distinguishes three outcomes:

| Fingerprint result | Startup action |
|---|---|
| Unavailable | Log an inconclusive check and keep the reachable engine |
| Matches the bundled fingerprint | Keep the engine |
| Positively differs | Stop the engine and launch its replacement |

The decisive code is this branch in [`EngineProcessController.start`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L195-L205), shown with logging omitted:

```swift
guard let runningFP else {
    // Log the inconclusive check.
    return
}
if bundledFP == runningFP {
    // Log the matching build.
    return
}
try stopRunningEngine(running)
```

Those returns exit the `withStartLock` closure. Execution still reaches the supervision setup after the closure; keeping an engine does not bypass subsequent liveness supervision.

**Worked example, taken from the new regression fixture.** The primary socket is reachable, forced restart is disabled, and a bundled fixture file contains `"bundled engine fixture"`. Its fingerprint can be computed, but the running engine’s fingerprint RPC returns `nil` every time. Assume `BOSS_ENGINE_CMD` is unset so version checking runs.

1. Both implementations discover the reachable socket, compute the bundled fingerprint, and make three fingerprint requests.
2. **Old behavior:** the matching-fingerprint condition fails because the result is `nil`. Boss logs an upgrade and calls `stopRunningEngine`. With this fixture’s successful shutdown/close responses, it then invokes the replacement launch handler.
3. **New behavior:** `guard let runningFP` fails. Boss logs `[engine version-check inconclusive]` and exits the startup closure without requesting shutdown or launching a replacement.

The observable result is pinned directly by the [new test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238):

```swift
XCTAssertEqual(
    fixture.socketControl.fingerprintRequests,
    Array(repeating: fixture.paths.socketPath, count: 3)
)
XCTAssertTrue(fixture.socketControl.shutdownRequests.isEmpty)
XCTAssertTrue(launchRecorder.socketPaths.isEmpty)
```

The fake returns `nil` immediately, so this tests the decision after unavailable responses, not actual timeout duration.

The useful contrasting case is a **known mismatch**: the existing `"stale-engine"` legacy-socket test still expects shutdown on the legacy endpoint and replacement on the primary endpoint. Preservation applies to uncertainty; confirmed mismatches still trigger replacement. See the [existing mismatch test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L208-L222).

**3. Major logic and architecture changes.** The existing separation remains: `EngineSupervisor` makes pure state-machine decisions, while `EngineProcessController` performs I/O, schedules recovery, and publishes state.

The supervisor gains a failure counter and an intermediate `.unreachable(consecutiveFailures:requiredFailures:)` action. The [new threshold gate](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L47-L65) sits before restart-budget consumption:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
let attempt = restartAttempts + 1
```

With the default threshold of three, failed ticks produce `unreachable(1/3)`, then `unreachable(2/3)`, then restart attempt 1 with its existing one-second backoff. This counts observations, rather than measuring an elapsed outage duration.

Several details matter when reviewing this state machine:

- A healthy tick immediately clears the failure streak. Replenishing an already-used restart budget still requires the existing healthy interval.
- `reset()` also clears the streak.
- Reaching the threshold clears the streak before checking the attempt budget, so subsequent recovery decisions require another streak.
- The default threshold is three and constructor values are clamped to at least one. The existing backoff schedule, six-attempt limit, one-second polling interval, and 60-second healthy-reset interval remain. There is no new environment-variable override for the threshold.

See the [policy configuration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L9-L51) and [complete supervisor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift).

The controller handles `.unreachable` by logging and returning, without scheduling work or publishing a new supervision state. Logs identify whether the observation came from the injected client-connection probe or socket discovery. Restart logs now describe consecutive unreachable ticks instead of asserting process exit. Probe selection itself is unchanged: an installed client probe supplies the answer; a false result does not trigger a second socket check. See [controller integration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L395-L433).

One boundary to keep in mind: ticks are skipped while a restart is pending. This change delays scheduling; it does not add cancellation when connectivity recovers during the backoff.

**4. Tests and supporting infrastructure.** Two tests are added:

- **Controller regression:** the worked example above verifies three unavailable fingerprint responses cause neither shutdown nor replacement.
- **Supervisor threshold:** three consecutive failed ticks produce two `.unreachable` actions followed by `.restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. All calls use the same timestamp, reinforcing that the threshold counts ticks. See the [new supervisor test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift#L74-L89).

Supporting changes are confined to the existing test fixtures and configuration. `FakeSocketControl.expectedFingerprint` becomes optional, and `Fixture` gains `fingerprintAvailable`, defaulting to `true`. This lets tests model a reachable socket independently from fingerprint availability while preserving existing fixture behavior. See the [updated fake and fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L291-L389).

Three existing budget/reset tests explicitly select threshold `1`, preserving their focus on budget exhaustion and replenishment. The new tests do not directly cover a healthy tick interrupting a partial failure streak or controller-level delayed scheduling. No build or test-runner configuration changes appear in the supplied diff.

The PR description lists Bazel library/test builds, `BossTestsShard3` execution, app/installer builds, and `checkleft run` as validation. I have not independently run those checks.

# PR #2886: Preserve engines when checks are inconclusive

This guide covers base `6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0` → head `68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4`. Links use revision-pinned source because exact diff anchors were not supplied.

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss could initiate engine replacement from evidence that did not establish a stale build or a dead process:

- **During startup**, an engine’s socket could be reachable while its fingerprint RPC returned no value. After three unsuccessful requests, the old implementation treated that uncertainty like a fingerprint mismatch and called `stopRunningEngine`.
- **During supervision**, a single failed liveness tick immediately consumed a restart attempt and scheduled recovery.

The first path could be particularly disruptive: the unchanged shutdown helper tries an RPC first, then can escalate to SIGTERM/SIGKILL if a suitable running engine PID is available and shutdown fails. The PR prevents an unavailable fingerprint from initiating that path. [Before: startup and shutdown logic](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

“Healthy” in the title is the motivation, not a newly verified property. The implementation preserves an engine discovered through socket reachability; it does not establish that all engine operations work.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change separates **unknown build identity**, **confirmed fingerprint mismatch**, and **repeated unreachability**:

| Evidence | Revised behavior |
|---|---|
| Running fingerprint unavailable after three attempts | Log an inconclusive check and preserve the discovered engine |
| Running fingerprint matches the bundle | Keep the existing engine |
| Returned fingerprint differs from the bundle | Stop the existing engine and proceed to launch |
| Failed supervision tick below the threshold | Record/log the failure without scheduling recovery |
| Failure streak reaches the threshold | Apply the existing restart budget and backoff |

The architecture remains split between `EngineProcessController`, which performs I/O and schedules work, and `EngineSupervisor`, which makes restart decisions. The policy gains `consecutiveFailureThreshold`, defaulting to **3** and clamped to at least **1**. The default polling interval remains one second; the threshold counts processed ticks, not elapsed seconds. No environment override for the new threshold is added. [Controller and policy](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift), [supervisor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift)

## 3. Implementation walkthrough and worked example

**Start with the fingerprint decision in `start(resetRestartBudget:)`.** Discovery and fingerprint acquisition are unchanged: after finding a reachable endpoint, the controller computes the bundled fingerprint and requests the running fingerprint up to three times, passing a three-second timeout each time. It stops retrying at the first non-`nil` response.

The decisive change is the early return for an unavailable fingerprint. Condensed pseudocode, with logging omitted:

```swift
guard let runningFP else { return }       // Newly preserves unknown builds
if bundledFP == runningFP { return }
try stopRunningEngine(running)
// Continue to launch.
```

These returns leave the `withStartLock` **closure**, not the enclosing `start` method. Execution still reaches the existing supervision setup unless supervision has been stopped. Thus preservation does not disable subsequent monitoring. [Core fix and surrounding control flow](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

The scope is deliberately narrower than “never replace an unresponsive engine.” Explicit `forceRestart` handling occurs before this check, and manual `restart()` retains its stop-and-launch behavior. Conversely, an inconclusive check can preserve an older build: matching the bundle is no longer required when the running fingerprint is unavailable. The unchanged comment describing retries before “treating non-response as a mismatch” is stale; the new guard determines the behavior.

**Worked example: reachable socket, unavailable fingerprint.** This uses the setup of the added `testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement`, with `BOSS_ENGINE_CMD` assumed unset so version checking runs:

- The primary socket is reachable.
- The fixture supplies a readable bundled file containing `"bundled engine fixture"`.
- `forceRestart` and `stopOnExit` are false.
- The fake fingerprint method returns `nil` on every request.
- The fake shutdown succeeds, `waitForClose` returns true, and a launch handler records calls and would return PID `4242`.

| Step | Base behavior | Head behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Discover engine | Finds the primary socket | Same |
| Request fingerprint | Three requests return `nil` | Same |
| Decide whether to replace | Falls through to the upgrade/shutdown path | Logs `version-check inconclusive` and returns from the lock closure |
| Observable calls in this fixture | One shutdown, followed by one launch | **No shutdown and no launch** |
| After the lock closure | Reaches supervision setup | Reaches supervision setup |

The new test directly asserts the three requests and absence of shutdown/launch calls. The base outcome above follows from tracing the old controller against the supplied fake; it is not a reported test execution. [Regression test and fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift), [old decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift), [new decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

The contrasting boundary remains a returned mismatch. The existing stale-legacy-engine test supplies `"stale-engine"` and asserts shutdown of the legacy endpoint followed by launch on the primary endpoint. Unknown identity and a differing fingerprint now take different branches.

**Next, read the supervisor’s failure-streak handling.** It adds `consecutiveFailures` and an internal `.unreachable` action. After incrementing the counter and checking whether the budget is already exhausted, it applies:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
```

Only after this gate does it calculate and consume the next restart attempt. A reachable tick immediately clears the failure streak; resetting the restart budget still requires the existing healthy interval, or an explicit `reset()`. Because reaching the threshold also clears the streak, subsequent restart attempts require another complete streak. The threshold likewise precedes the transition to `.gaveUp`. [Supervisor state transitions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift)

**Finally, follow the action back into the controller.** The controller still uses the injected liveness probe when present, otherwise socket discovery. A false injected result does **not** trigger a second socket check. The new `.unreachable` branch logs the signal source and failure count, then returns without scheduling work or emitting a new supervision state.

At the threshold, the log describes repeated unreachability instead of asserting that the engine exited. Existing delayed recovery calls `start(resetRestartBudget: false)`, which rediscovers the engine and applies the startup logic above; scheduling recovery does not guarantee replacement. Polling checks are skipped while a restart is pending. [Controller integration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added: two tests.**

- `testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement` asserts exactly three fingerprint requests to the primary socket, no shutdown requests, and no launch calls.
- `testDebouncesSingleUnreachableTickBeforeSchedulingRestart` asserts two `.unreachable` actions with counts `1/3` and `2/3`, followed by `.restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. All calls use the same timestamp, reinforcing that this is a tick-count threshold.

[Controller regression](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift), [supervisor regression](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift)

**Modified: three existing budget tests.** Exhaustion across dead ticks, replenishment after a healthy interval, and immediate restoration by `reset()` now explicitly set `consecutiveFailureThreshold: 1`. Their existing assertions remain focused on budget behavior rather than the new debounce. No tests are removed. [Modified tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift)

**Fixture changes:** `FakeSocketControl.expectedFingerprint` becomes optional, and `Fixture` gains `fingerprintAvailable`, defaulting to true. Setting it false models a reachable socket whose fingerprint RPC yields no value. Existing request recording and launch injection are reused. No build or configuration changes appear in the supplied comparison. [Fixture changes](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift)

**Coverage limits:** the fingerprint fake returns immediately, so the regression verifies the decision after missing responses, not actual timeout timing. The added supervisor test checks the action sequence, not controller timer scheduling, logging, or a recovery tick interrupting a partial failure streak.

The PR description reports Bazel builds for the app library, `BossTestsShard3`, `Boss`, and installer release; a Bazel test run of `BossTestsShard3`; and `checkleft run`. This guide is based on the supplied source comparison; I did not run those checks.

# PR #2886: Preserve reachable engines when checks are inconclusive

This guide covers the complete comparison from `6f8ca35153d0` to `68e51b6cfd5c`. Links use revision-pinned source locations because validated line-level PR diff URLs were unavailable.

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss could initiate engine recovery on insufficient evidence in two places:

- **At startup:** after discovering a reachable engine, three unsuccessful fingerprint RPCs led to the same shutdown-and-replacement path as a confirmed fingerprint mismatch.
- **During supervision:** one failed liveness tick immediately scheduled a restart attempt.

These signals do not establish that the engine has exited or is running an outdated build. Socket reachability only establishes that a connection succeeds; fingerprint retrieval separately requires a suitable RPC response. A missing fingerprint can also reflect an unexpected response type or absent fingerprint field. See the [socket and fingerprint helpers](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossEnginePaths.swift#L256-L291).

The startup behavior was particularly consequential: replacement enters the existing shutdown machinery, which can escalate from RPC shutdown to validated PID-based signals.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change introduces two separate protections:

| Decision | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reachable engine, fingerprint unavailable after three attempts | Attempt replacement | Keep the discovered engine |
| Fingerprints available and different | Attempt replacement | Same |
| Failed supervision tick | Immediately schedule recovery | Require three consecutive failures by default |

The architecture remains split between **`EngineSupervisor`**, which makes pure state-machine decisions, and **`EngineProcessController`**, which probes, logs, schedules work, and manages processes.

The new contract favors preserving a reachable engine when its version is unknown. It does **not** prove that engine is healthy or matches the bundle.

## 3. Implementation walkthrough and worked example

**Start with the fingerprint decision in `EngineProcessController.start`.** The existing loop still makes up to three fingerprint requests, each receiving a three-second timeout argument, and stops at the first non-`nil` result. The decisive addition is:

```swift
guard let runningFP else {
    emit("[engine version-check inconclusive] running fingerprint unavailable after \(fingerprintAttempts) attempts bundled=\(bundledFP) — keeping reachable \(describe(running))")
    return
}
```

Only an available, unequal fingerprint now reaches `stopRunningEngine`. Equal fingerprints retain the engine as before. See the [core branch](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L205).

Two control-flow details matter for review:

- This `return` exits the **`withStartLock` closure**, so `start` still proceeds to enable supervision unless supervision has been stopped. It does not abandon supervision.
- Reachability was established during discovery; the new branch does not recheck it after the fingerprint attempts.

The [surrounding startup path](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L142-L219) preserves existing exceptions: forced restart acts earlier, `BOSS_ENGINE_CMD` or no bundled engine skips comparison, and inability to fingerprint the bundled file throws. The unchanged comment about eventually “treating non-response as a mismatch” is now stale; the guard defines the behavior.

**Worked example: a reachable engine returns no fingerprint.** This scenario comes directly from the [new controller regression test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238).

Relevant fixture state:

- The primary socket reports reachable.
- A temporary bundled file contains `"bundled engine fixture"` and can be fingerprinted.
- `fingerprintAvailable: false` makes every fingerprint request return `nil`.
- Forced restart is disabled; shutdown and launch calls are recorded. The fake shutdown succeeds and `waitForClose` returns `true`.

Assuming `BOSS_ENGINE_CMD` is unset so comparison runs, the trace is:

| Step | Base revision | Head revision |
|---|---|---|
| Discover engine | Primary socket is reachable | Same |
| Retrieve fingerprint | Three requests return `nil` | Same |
| Decide | Log upgrade and call shutdown | Log inconclusive check and return from lock closure |
| Observable result with this fixture | One shutdown request, then one launch on the primary socket | No shutdown requests and no launch calls |

The old result follows from the [base replacement branch](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L215) and fixture behavior; the new result is explicitly asserted by the added test. This example uses immediate fake `nil` responses, not real three-second timeouts.

The useful contrasting case is a returned `"stale-engine"` fingerprint: the unchanged [legacy-engine replacement test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L207-L222) still expects shutdown on the legacy socket and replacement launch on the primary socket.

**Next, read the supervisor’s failure counter.** `EngineRestartPolicy` adds `consecutiveFailureThreshold`, defaulting to three and clamped to at least one. No environment override is added for this field. See the [policy definition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L9-L51).

Before consuming a restart attempt, the supervisor now checks:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
```

The [complete state transition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L25-L65) makes the failures consecutive: a successful tick clears the counter immediately. Reaching the threshold also clears it, so subsequent attempts require another failure streak. Restart-budget replenishment remains separate and requires the existing healthy interval—60 seconds by default.

With an unused default budget, three failed calls produce `.unreachable(1, 3)`, `.unreachable(2, 3)`, then `.restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. This is a **tick-count threshold**, not an elapsed-time guarantee.

**Finally, follow the action back into the controller.** The [controller integration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L393-L447) logs intermediate failures without scheduling work or emitting a new supervision state. On threshold crossing, it emits `.restarting` and schedules the existing delayed recovery path.

The liveness source is unchanged: production [wires in `EngineClient.isReachable`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1215-L1228), which tracks [connection state](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineClient.swift#L107-L136). Socket discovery is used only when no probe is installed; a false client result does not trigger a second socket check.

Logs now name the source on intermediate failures and describe consecutive unreachability instead of asserting “engine exited.” Scheduled recovery still calls `start(resetRestartBudget: false)`, so it rediscovers the engine and applies the fingerprint rules rather than unconditionally replacing it.

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added: two tests.**

- [`testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238) asserts exactly three fingerprint requests, no shutdown, and no launch.
- [`testDebouncesSingleUnreachableTickBeforeSchedulingRestart`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift#L75-L90) asserts two intermediate unreachable actions followed by attempt one with a one-second delay. All calls use the same timestamp, confirming count-based decision logic.

**Modified: three existing policy tests.** Budget exhaustion, healthy-interval replenishment, and explicit reset now set `consecutiveFailureThreshold: 1`, preserving their original immediate-retry assertions while isolating budget behavior. See the [modified tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift#L32-L73). No tests were removed.

**Fixture changes:** the fake socket controller’s expected fingerprint becomes optional, and `Fixture` gains `fingerprintAvailable`, defaulting to `true`. This allows missing responses without changing existing matching/mismatching fixtures. See the [fake](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L291-L331) and [fixture setup](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L347-L408).

There are no build/configuration changes. Both test files already belong to the existing [Shard3 catch-all source glob](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L278-L291).

# PR #2886: Preserve engines when checks are inconclusive

This guide covers base `6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0` → head `68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4`. Links use revision-pinned source because exact diff anchors were not supplied.

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss could initiate engine replacement from evidence that did not establish a stale build or a dead process:

- **During startup**, an engine’s socket could be reachable while its fingerprint RPC returned no value. After three unsuccessful requests, the old implementation treated that uncertainty like a fingerprint mismatch and called `stopRunningEngine`.
- **During supervision**, a single failed liveness tick immediately consumed a restart attempt and scheduled recovery.

The first path could be particularly disruptive: the unchanged shutdown helper tries an RPC first, then can escalate to SIGTERM/SIGKILL if a suitable running engine PID is available and shutdown fails. The PR prevents an unavailable fingerprint from initiating that path. [Before: startup and shutdown logic](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

“Healthy” in the title is the motivation, not a newly verified property. The implementation preserves an engine discovered through socket reachability; it does not establish that all engine operations work.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change separates **unknown build identity**, **confirmed fingerprint mismatch**, and **repeated unreachability**:

| Evidence | Revised behavior |
|---|---|
| Running fingerprint unavailable after three attempts | Log an inconclusive check and preserve the discovered engine |
| Running fingerprint matches the bundle | Keep the existing engine |
| Returned fingerprint differs from the bundle | Stop the existing engine and proceed to launch |
| Failed supervision tick below the threshold | Record/log the failure without scheduling recovery |
| Failure streak reaches the threshold | Apply the existing restart budget and backoff |

The architecture remains split between `EngineProcessController`, which performs I/O and schedules work, and `EngineSupervisor`, which makes restart decisions. The policy gains `consecutiveFailureThreshold`, defaulting to **3** and clamped to at least **1**. The default polling interval remains one second; the threshold counts processed ticks, not elapsed seconds. No environment override for the new threshold is added. [Controller and policy](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift), [supervisor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift)

## 3. Implementation walkthrough and worked example

**Start with the fingerprint decision in `start(resetRestartBudget:)`.** Discovery and fingerprint acquisition are unchanged: after finding a reachable endpoint, the controller computes the bundled fingerprint and requests the running fingerprint up to three times, passing a three-second timeout each time. It stops retrying at the first non-`nil` response.

The decisive change is the early return for an unavailable fingerprint. Condensed pseudocode, with logging omitted:

```swift
guard let runningFP else { return }       // Newly preserves unknown builds
if bundledFP == runningFP { return }
try stopRunningEngine(running)
// Continue to launch.
```

These returns leave the `withStartLock` **closure**, not the enclosing `start` method. Execution still reaches the existing supervision setup unless supervision has been stopped. Thus preservation does not disable subsequent monitoring. [Core fix and surrounding control flow](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

The scope is deliberately narrower than “never replace an unresponsive engine.” Explicit `forceRestart` handling occurs before this check, and manual `restart()` retains its stop-and-launch behavior. Conversely, an inconclusive check can preserve an older build: matching the bundle is no longer required when the running fingerprint is unavailable. The unchanged comment describing retries before “treating non-response as a mismatch” is stale; the new guard determines the behavior.

**Worked example: reachable socket, unavailable fingerprint.** This uses the setup of the added `testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement`, with `BOSS_ENGINE_CMD` assumed unset so version checking runs:

- The primary socket is reachable.
- The fixture supplies a readable bundled file containing `"bundled engine fixture"`.
- `forceRestart` and `stopOnExit` are false.
- The fake fingerprint method returns `nil` on every request.
- The fake shutdown succeeds, `waitForClose` returns true, and a launch handler records calls and would return PID `4242`.

| Step | Base behavior | Head behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Discover engine | Finds the primary socket | Same |
| Request fingerprint | Three requests return `nil` | Same |
| Decide whether to replace | Falls through to the upgrade/shutdown path | Logs `version-check inconclusive` and returns from the lock closure |
| Observable calls in this fixture | One shutdown, followed by one launch | **No shutdown and no launch** |
| After the lock closure | Reaches supervision setup | Reaches supervision setup |

The new test directly asserts the three requests and absence of shutdown/launch calls. The base outcome above follows from tracing the old controller against the supplied fake; it is not a reported test execution. [Regression test and fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift), [old decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift), [new decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

The contrasting boundary remains a returned mismatch. The existing stale-legacy-engine test supplies `"stale-engine"` and asserts shutdown of the legacy endpoint followed by launch on the primary endpoint. Unknown identity and a differing fingerprint now take different branches.

**Next, read the supervisor’s failure-streak handling.** It adds `consecutiveFailures` and an internal `.unreachable` action. After incrementing the counter and checking whether the budget is already exhausted, it applies:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
```

Only after this gate does it calculate and consume the next restart attempt. A reachable tick immediately clears the failure streak; resetting the restart budget still requires the existing healthy interval, or an explicit `reset()`. Because reaching the threshold also clears the streak, subsequent restart attempts require another complete streak. The threshold likewise precedes the transition to `.gaveUp`. [Supervisor state transitions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift)

**Finally, follow the action back into the controller.** The controller still uses the injected liveness probe when present, otherwise socket discovery. A false injected result does **not** trigger a second socket check. The new `.unreachable` branch logs the signal source and failure count, then returns without scheduling work or emitting a new supervision state.

At the threshold, the log describes repeated unreachability instead of asserting that the engine exited. Existing delayed recovery calls `start(resetRestartBudget: false)`, which rediscovers the engine and applies the startup logic above; scheduling recovery does not guarantee replacement. Polling checks are skipped while a restart is pending. [Controller integration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift)

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added: two tests.**

- `testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement` asserts exactly three fingerprint requests to the primary socket, no shutdown requests, and no launch calls.
- `testDebouncesSingleUnreachableTickBeforeSchedulingRestart` asserts two `.unreachable` actions with counts `1/3` and `2/3`, followed by `.restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. All calls use the same timestamp, reinforcing that this is a tick-count threshold.

[Controller regression](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift), [supervisor regression](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift)

**Modified: three existing budget tests.** Exhaustion across dead ticks, replenishment after a healthy interval, and immediate restoration by `reset()` now explicitly set `consecutiveFailureThreshold: 1`. Their existing assertions remain focused on budget behavior rather than the new debounce. No tests are removed. [Modified tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift)

**Fixture changes:** `FakeSocketControl.expectedFingerprint` becomes optional, and `Fixture` gains `fingerprintAvailable`, defaulting to true. Setting it false models a reachable socket whose fingerprint RPC yields no value. Existing request recording and launch injection are reused. No build or configuration changes appear in the supplied comparison. [Fixture changes](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift)

**Coverage limits:** the fingerprint fake returns immediately, so the regression verifies the decision after missing responses, not actual timeout timing. The added supervisor test checks the action sequence, not controller timer scheduling, logging, or a recovery tick interrupting a partial failure streak.

The PR description reports Bazel builds for the app library, `BossTestsShard3`, `Boss`, and installer release; a Bazel test run of `BossTestsShard3`; and `checkleft run`. This guide is based on the supplied source comparison; I did not run those checks.
